new_statements.quote: Five tone classes L M H LH ML were confirmed by classifying CV, CVC, CCVC, CVCV and CVCVC words according to their tone, as shown in full below. Words sometimes varied between the LH class and the M class or (for one speaker) between the LH class and the L class. [p.6] ... With these effects, the system reduces to an underlying two-tone L-H system with four underlying melodies /L/, /H/, /LH/ or /LHL/, of which the latter two instantiate downstep after a floating L, producing [ꜜH] and [ꜜHL] respectively. [p.14]

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (15 pp., Word 2016 text layer;.txt via extracted text). Both quoted sentences are present word-for-word: 'Five tone classes L M H LH ML were confirmed by classifying CV, CVC, CCVC, CVCV and CVCVC words according to their tone, as shown in full below. Words sometimes varied between the LH class and the M class or (for one speaker) between the LH class and the L class.' opens sec. 6 Tones and sits on the page carrying printed number 6 (txt lines 251-254); 'With these effects, the system reduces to an underlying two-tone L-H system with four underlying melodies /L/, /H/, /LH/ or /LHL/, of which the latter two instantiate downstep after a floating L, producing [ꜜH] and [ꜜHL] respectively…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bijim is a tone language: lexical items fall into five surface tone classes (L, M, H, LH rising, ML falling) which Norton analyses as an underlying two-tone /L, H/ system with floating-L downstep. The source says nothing about word stress or accent; no accessible source states where stress falls or whether stress exists.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone classes LH and M (and for one speaker LH and L) vary; tone on syllabic nasals not assessed (p.13).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone on citation-form words elicited from a Blench 600-item wordlist in a participatory workshop with five speakers (Gambar, Aruti, Dukli, Yang villages); no phrase-level prosody, no stress discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Norton 2019 and the dictionary describe the Bijim variety [bij-17997] with speakers from Gambar, Aruti and Yang (Tafawa Balewa LGA, Bauchi State) and Dukli (Gindiri area, Plateau State); after ISO change request 2020-035 these lects are Bijim [jbm] = biji1246 (Decker et al. 2021 lgcode: Kaduk = Luggere, Gambar, Dukli Bauchi = Bijim [jbm]). The sister lects Kadung/Kwanka/Kwaŋ [dkg] and Tiyaa/Ya/Boi [tyy] are separate languages (Glottolog vagh1250 sisters); Blench 2007 (fetched sources) describes Kadung, not Bijim. Glottolog still lists Blench 2022 under the name 'Vaghat' = Bijim.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Luther Hon, Julius Dabet, Benard Abraham & Innocent Jonah. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Bijim [jbm] Language of Plateau and Bauchi States, Nigeria, with Mention of the Kadung [dkg] and Tiyaa [tyy] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-033. Dallas: SIL International, 72 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory of Bijim-Kadung-Tiyaa' (p.14) is 'initial, cursory observations': consonant table, labialization/palatalization; sec. 6.6 phonological variation between varieties. Appendix E (p.42): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Wordlists (App. E-F) carry tone diacritics. No stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Riepe, Christina (SIL Nigeria). 2020. Change Request 2020-035: split [bij] Vaghat-Ya-Bijim-Legeri into Bijim [jbm], Kadung [dkg], Tiyaa [tyy]. 6 pp.
sources.note: Identity document only: lexical-similarity matrix (Luggere, Bijim, Kwanka/Mwel Kadung), village visits 2016-2020; announces the Decker et al. survey report. No phonology.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell J. 2019 [research 10-13 Oct 2018]. Bijim Linguistics Consultant Report. Bukuru: SIL Nigeria / TCNN, 15 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives item 84252; report dated 27 Feb 2019).
sources.note: Primary phonology (participatory). Sec. 6 Tones (p.6): five tone classes L M H LH ML on CV/CVC/CCVC/CVCV/CVCVC words; sec. 10 (p.14): reduces to an underlying two-tone L-H system with four melodies /L/ /H/ /LH/ /LHL/ and downstep; sec. 9 (p.10): CCVC syllable structure. No statement on stress or accent anywhere (the only hit for 'stress' is the gloss of the noun ɗaka 'stress', p.6).

sources.citation: Norton, Russell (comp.), with Bulus Foli, Joseph Gomar, Joshua Mungi, Yohana Jiniya & Ibrahim Gwalang. 2018. A First Bijim-English Dictionary: 559 words. SIL Nigeria (CC BY-SA), 11 pp.
sources.note: Front-matter 'Tone' note (p.1): double vowel = high tone, h after vowel = low tone, VVh = rising tone, mid unmarked; tone marks used on short CV words and on longer minimal pairs. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. The Kwaŋ language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft ms. circulated for comment, Cambridge, 28 pp. (printout 5 Sep 2007). [Sister language Kwaŋ/Kwanka = Kadung [dkg], not Bijim.]
sources.note: Sec. 3 Phonology has vowels and consonants; sec. 3.3 'Tones' (p.3) is an empty heading. Wordlist is tone-marked. Nothing on stress; and it describes Kadung, not Bijim (Norton 2019 p.2: Bijim speakers 'understand some but not all' of Kaɗung).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. Tarok and related languages of east-central Nigeria: nomenclature and subclassification. Draft ms., 21 pp. (printout 22 Oct 2004).
sources.note: Does not mention Bijim, Vaghat or Legeri at all (predates their Tarokoid assignment); tone remarks concern Tarok noun-class tone raising only. Nothing on stress.
